# Captain Jim

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventy-six  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c8 P59](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0059), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P14](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0014), [v4 c39 P16](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0016)</sub>
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v4 c24 P41](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0041)</sub>
- **Role:** Former sea captain and lighthouse keeper  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c24 P41](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0041), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain Jim  <sub>[v4 c8 P59](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0059)</sub>; Captain Boyd  <sub>[v4 c24 P33](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0033)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Uncle Jim  <sub>[v4 c24 P35](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0035)</sub>

## Appearance

Captain Jim is described as a tall, rugged, silver-haired man with deep-set blue eyes and big brown hands. As he aged, his head whitened swiftly and he became bent and frail, moving more slowly and haltingly. In his youth and moments of intense emotion, his eyes burned with brilliant fire.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P59](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0059), [v4 c9 P59](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0059), [v4 c24 P30](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0030), [v4 c39 P4](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0004), [v4 c39 P10](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0010)_

## Personality

Captain Jim is a high-souled, placid, cheerful, and compassionate man known for his simple-souled hospitality and deep wisdom. He possesses a born talent for storytelling, painting vivid scenes with gestures, facial expressions, and humor. Though exceptionally patient and almost impossible to anger, he is fiercely defensive of women and incapable of tolerating disrespect or cruelty toward them or animals. He remains deeply reflective, reverent, and youthful at heart despite a lifetime of hardship.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P59](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0059), [v4 c8 P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061), [v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038), [v4 c9 P48](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0048), [v4 c9 P50](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0050), [v4 c9 P51](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0051), [v4 c9 P59](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0059)_

## History

Captain Jim spent the majority of his life at sea, traveling to remote corners of the world and surviving wild adventures including mutinies, shipwrecks, Malay pirates, and shipwreck on the Magdalens. Five years before retiring to the Four Winds Point lighthouse, he ceased his ocean voyages and settled into the life of a lightkeeper, living simply with his cat, Matey, whom he had rescued from freezing. He formed close bonds with local residents, including Elizabeth Russell, Miss Cornelia Bryant, and later Anne and Gilbert Blythe. When Owen Ford visited Four Winds, Captain Jim shared his treasured 'life-book' manuscript with him. Owen Ford adapted the manuscript into a published book titled 'The Life-Book of Captain Jim', listing Captain Jim as a collaborator. On the evening after receiving his published book, Captain Jim celebrated with Anne and Leslie Moore before passing away peacefully in his home.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038), [v4 c9 P42](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0042), [v4 c9 P55](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0055), [v4 c9 P56](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0056), [v4 c24 P30](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0030), [v4 c24 P34](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0034), [v4 c39 P0](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0000), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005), [v4 c39 P11](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0011), [v4 c39 P16](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0016)_
